request: Analyze GSE235042 for PMID 41946794 (4-Phenylbutyrate mitigates renal pathology linked to ER stress related pathways in C57BL/6J mice with hindlimb unloading.): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.

final.assay: bulk RNA-seq (Illumina HiSeq 4000, paired-end, HISAT2 mm10), mouse kidney
final.organism: Mus musculus, male C57BL/6J, 4 months old
final.sample_inclusion: 3 kidneys per group sequenced (S2.4.p1) out of n=10 mice/group in the animal study (S2.2.p1): GC, HU (vehicle PBS), HU-t (HU + 4-PBA 100 mg/kg/d i.p.)

grp: HU (hindlimb unloaded, 3 weeks tail suspension, vehicle)

final.primary_estimand: Effect of 3 weeks of hindlimb unloading (mechanical disuse / physical inactivity model; the physical-activity axis of this paper, the inverse of loading/exercise) on the kidney transcriptome: HU vs GC. 4-PBA contrasts are drug effects, secondary.
planned_contrasts: HU vs GC (S3.3.p1, Fig. 4a; paper: 6628 DEGs, 4592 up / 2036 down)
HU-t vs HU (S3.3.p1, Fig. 4b; paper: 3543 DEGs, 1096 up / 2447 down)
HU-t vs GC (S3.3.p1, Fig. 4c; paper: 1114 DEGs, 890 up / 224 down)
final.repeated_measure_unit: none; one kidney per mouse, independent animals
final.normalization: read counts -> FPKM for PCA/heatmaps (S2.7.p1); DESeq2 on quantification data (S2.8.p1)
final.paper_method: DESeq2 pairwise comparisons on read counts (S2.8.p1; S2.4.p1 mentions DESeq2/EdgeR)
final.paper_results: HU vs GC: ECM organization/ECM-receptor interaction, olfactory transduction, collagen degradation, muscle contraction up; mitochondrial protein complex, OXPHOS/TCA, SLC-mediated transport down (S3.3.p2, S3.4.p1, S3.5.p1, S4.p7). HU-t vs HU: PPAR signaling, peroxisome, SLC transport, ROS detox up; ECM, RNA splicing down.

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: S2.2.p1/S2.4.p1 define the three groups and 3 sequenced replicates each; S2.8.p1 states DESeq2 with BH-adjusted p < 0.05 (the 'log2FoldChange > 0' clause only splits up vs down, no magnitude cutoff); S3.3.p1 gives the three DEG counts. No exercise arm exists; the paper's physical-activity manipulation is hindlimb unloading (disuse), which S5.p1 frames as a model of bed rest and lack of physical activity. HU vs GC is therefore the activity estimand (direction: inactivity relative to normal cage activity).

checks: metadata series_id GSE235042, 9 GSMs, kidney, male C57BL/6J, HiSeq 4000, 3 per group (Ground control / Hindlimb Unloaded / Hindlimb Unloaded/PBA Treated) as in S2.4.p1
GEO data_processing text is identical to paper S2.6-S2.7 (HISAT2, FPKM)

ownership.reasoning: Paper data availability S10.p1 cites GSE235042; group sizes, tissue, strain and processing text match.

alignment.reasoning: Matrix columns (MC1_K, U4_K, UP3_Kidney, ...) are the first comma field of GEO 'description' (inspect alignment_keys: 9/9). Group from characteristics treatment; MC=control, U=unloaded, UP=unloaded+PBA prefixes agree.

matrix.reasoning: Only deposited matrix is GSE235042_Processed_data.txt.gz: non-integer values (integer fraction 0.66 is driven by zeros), column sums differ 0.29M-1.9M, data_processing and S2.7.p1 say read counts were normalized to FPKM and the file holds 'normalized abundance'. No raw counts and no RAW tar (supplementary_file NONE). Paper ran DESeq2 on counts; that input is not available.

design.reasoning: One factor with three levels and one control; one model on all 9 samples with the paper's three pairwise contrasts (S3.3.p1, Fig. 4a-c), never pooling levels. HU vs GC is the primary activity (unloading/disuse) estimand; 4-PBA contrasts are drug effects kept as secondary. n=3 per group (small; reported as such). Estimand is causal (randomized, S2.2.p1) but it is disuse, not exercise.

candidates.value: pool HU and HUt vs GC as 'unloaded'
candidates.reason_rejected: 4-PBA changes the kidney transcriptome per paper; pooling mixes drug and unloading.

the paper's physical-activity manipulation (hindlimb unloading vs ground control) is present with 3 vs 3 animals; analyzed as the inactivity side of the activity axis, as done for other HU studies in this run.

covariance.reasoning: Independent animals, one kidney each; no batch, sex (all male) or lane information in GEO; nothing to block on. Sex genes: Xist ~0 and Ddx3y expressed in all 9, consistent with all-male.

paper_route.reason: only FPKM deposited; no raw counts or RAW tar in GEO; DESeq2 requires counts

deviations: limma on log2(FPKM+1) instead of DESeq2 on counts
low-expression filter FPKM >= 1 in >= 3 samples (not stated in paper)

method.reasoning: Matrix policy: FPKM -> log2(x+1) -> limma. One joint model over the three groups so all contrasts share the variance estimate. Filter genes with FPKM >= 1 in at least 3 samples (one group's worth) to remove the many all-zero genes in a 54k-feature table.

final.deviation_note: Paper rule BH FDR < 0.05 applied to limma on log2(FPKM+1) instead of DESeq2 on counts. Audit adds |log2FC| > 1 for comparison only.

threshold.reasoning: S2.8.p1: 'Genes with an adjusted p < 0.05 were assigned as significantly differentially expressed genes'; the 'log2 Fold change > 0' clause classifies direction, no magnitude cutoff.

caveats: No exercise arm: the activity contrast is hindlimb unloading (disuse) vs ground control, i.e. the inactivity direction; do not read it as an exercise effect.
Paper's DESeq2-on-counts route blocked (FPKM only); limma on log2(FPKM+1) is a declared deviation, so counts are not expected to match.
Paper text 'control mice vs. hindlimb unloaded mice ... 4592 upregulated' is ambiguous in direction; compared assuming up = higher in HU (Fig. 4a 'HU vs. GC').
Paper's DEG totals (6628 of the expressed genome at n=3) are unusually large.

study.reasoning: Counts from S3.3.p1; the paper names no individual genes, only pathways.

discrepancies.paper: n=10 mice/group in animal study (S2.2.p1); GEO treatment_protocol says n=6-8
discrepancies.data: 3 per group sequenced, consistent with S2.4.p1

executions.name: joint
executions.reasoning: One limma model ~grp on log2(FPKM+1), three pairwise contrasts as in the paper; HU vs GC is the primary activity contrast.

enrichment.reasoning: paper reports GO/KEGG/Reactome for HU vs GC (ECM up, mitochondria/OXPHOS down); GSEA Hallmark gives the signed comparison
secondary drug contrast; signed pathway check against paper's ECM down / peroxisome-PPAR up
